findings.where: Motion sketch panel at the foot of the page, at both widths: its full-width lavender fill
findings.fault: The motion panel is a large block of saturated lavender. That colour is not in the palette the tile itself declares (paper, grey, blue, pad yellow), and it is not in the house colours. When you squint, it is the loudest field on the page and outweighs the hero's pad-yellow strip and the article. The tile says 'one ground, an ink and at most one accent', with yellow kept for the address alone, and then breaks that in its own specimen. It also brings in a colour that reads as playful rather than legal.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges whether this direction is the house blue and grey on a quiet paper. A purple slab makes the tile look like it has a second, unexplained accent, so v1's restraint reads as broken. Mark could also take it as a colour he never asked for.

findings.where: Article specimen: the subheads 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?' and 'Download', at both widths
findings.fault: The subheads are set in a heavy, wide, black grotesque. It is a third face, outside the stated type pair, which gives Newsreader 500 for subheads. At a squint these two short lines are the darkest type in the article, darker than its body and nearly as loud as its title. The heavy wide sans also brings a tech or startup tone into a page set to read like a legal journal.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader going through Mark's article sees the subheads shout over the argument. The founder asked for serious, refined type with nothing that reads as 'in-your-face techy', and would also see that the tile's type spec and its own specimen disagree.

findings.where: Article specimen's Download item and the motion panel below it: at phone width the panel starts right under the 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' line, and on desktop it starts just under the download link
findings.fault: There is almost no space between the article's download item and the lavender motion panel. By proximity the PDF link reads as the top of the motion panel, or as cut off by it, instead of as the closing part of the article. The article has no clear end, and the next specimen begins mid-thought.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading the article specimen as 'the product' (depth after the first look): the PDF list looks like an afterthought crushed against an unrelated panel, not the article's proper close.
